content.text: Change the background color of the snake's tongue to #e03131 (red).
I'll help you change the snake's tongue background color. Let me first take a screenshot to see the current state of the page.

I can see a snake drawn on what appears to be an Excalidraw canvas. The snake has:
- A body made of several ellipses
- A head (circle) on the right with two eyes
- A tongue - the forked shape on the far right (the two crossed/split ellipses)

The tongue is the forked shape on the right side. Let me click on it to select it.

I've selected one part of the tongue (one of the forked ellipses). The tongue appears to be made of two ellipses that form the fork shape. Let me select both parts of the tongue. First, let me also select the other tongue part by holding Shift and clicking it.

It looks like the shift-click deselected the first one and selected the other tongue part instead. The shift text parameter may not have held the shift key properly. Let me use the proper approach - I'll click on the first tongue part, then use shift+click to add the second part.

Let me click on the first tongue ellipse (the upper fork).
Now let me shift+click on the second tongue part to add it to the selection. I'll use the key hold approach for shift.
Browser action failed: Keyboard.press: Unknown key: "shift"
Let me check the current selection state first with a screenshot.

The upper tongue part is currently selected. The tongue has two forked parts. To select both, I'll do a drag-selection around just the tongue area. But that risks catching the body ellipse. 

Actually, a cleaner approach: let me first set the background color for this selected part, then select the other part and do the same. But the "Background" swatches don't include #e03131. I need to open the custom color picker.

Let me first apply the background to the currently selected tongue part. Since #e03131 is a specific red, I need to click on the background color swatch to open the custom picker. Let me click the leftmost background swatch area to open the color options.
The color picker is open with a "Hex code" input field showing "transparent". Let me type the hex code #e03131 into that field. First let me clear it and enter the value.

The triple-click didn't fully clear the field. The hex field now shows "ranspae03131" - the "transparent" text wasn't cleared before typing. I need to clear the field completely. Let me click in the field, select all, and delete first.
Browser action failed: Keyboard.press: Unknown key: "ctrl"
The hex field is now cleared (showing just "#"). Now let me type the hex code.

The hex code #e03131 has been applied. The upper part of the tongue now shows red fill, and the background swatch in the panel shows the red color. The hex field confirms "e03131".

Now I need to apply the same color to the second (lower) part of the tongue. Let me close this color picker first and select the other tongue part. Let me click on the canvas empty area to close the picker, then select the lower tongue part.
Now let me select the lower tongue part.

The upper tongue part is now red. I've now selected the lower tongue part (I can see the selection handles on the lower fork). The Background swatch shows transparent again for this element. Let me open the color picker and apply the red color. Since the red color is now in the recently used swatches (rightmost swatch shows red), but currently it shows transparent. Let me click the background custom color area.
The color picker is open again with "transparent" in the hex field. Let me clear it and enter the hex code.
Both parts of the snake's tongue are now filled with the red color #e03131. The complete forked tongue is now red. Let me close the color picker and take a final screenshot to confirm the result.

The task is complete. The snake's tongue—the forked shape at the far right of the drawing—now has a red background color (#e03131). Both parts of the forked tongue are filled with the red color, creating a nice contrast against the black-outlined body and head of the snake.

Summary of what I did:
1. Selected each part of the snake's forked tongue (it was made of two ellipses)
2. Opened the Background color picker
3. Entered the hex code `e03131` in the hex code field
4. Applied it to both forked parts of the tongue

The snake now has a bright red tongue as requested!
